history.note: Opened with rules 27, which delivered land supply: hearths feed four hexes and twice as far along a road, enemies and sieges cut the line, and a force of three or more companies outside supply wastes away and rests badly. Ports and depots, supply costs, trade routes, tax policy, treaty access and persistent naval operations remain.

Rules 28 added built depots: a company raises one for forty coin, it feeds half a hearth's reach, it costs two coin a turn, depots stand three hexes apart, and any enemy that walks onto one razes it. Ports, supply costs in resources, trade routes, tax policy and treaty access remain.

Rules 29 drew supply on the map and let a realm pull its own depot down, closing an upkeep obligation rules 28 had made permanent. Teaching the AI to play supply was attempted three times and reverted each time: every version shifted campaign length outside its intended band, so it must move together with a deliberate re-tune of the pacing windows.

Rules 29 drew supply on the map, let a realm pull down its own depot, and gave the AI depot building. AI depot raiding, ports, supply costs in resources, trade routes, tax policy and treaty access remain.

The AI now raids enemy depots as a target of opportunity - within three hexes and weighted below engaging an enemy force. The first cut ranged eight hexes at four times the pull of an enemy army and pushed the headline campaign from 388 to 446 turns as both sides rebuilt the same posts; the tuned version holds it at 389 while still razing 238 depots. No rules, save or content change. Ports, supply costs in resources, trade routes, tax policy and treaty access remain.

Rules 30 carried a harbour hearth's supply line out over the water, so a fleet or a landing near a friendly coast is fed without building a post, and rewrote the search as two clean passes rather than one whose water-crossing depended on which line won a tie. Purely additive: the headline campaign still measures 389 turns. Fleets remain exempt from supply entirely; removing that, supply costs in resources, trade routes, tax policy and treaty access remain.

Fixed a latent AI accounting bug: the turn budget was computed from the treasury without subtracting the arcane survey, depot and patronage subsidy already paid in the same pass, so the planner could commit coin it had spent. Fleet supply provisions were built, tested and measured but not shipped - they put the headline campaign at 427 turns on eight provision turns and 412 on sixteen against 388 without them, because naval invasions fail when the AI does not plan around fleet supply. Shipping needs AI naval staging measured back into band, or a deliberate Epic re-price with the pace pack frozen.

Implemented and verified locally at rules/save 31: eight provision turns, shared hull/passenger attrition, harbour resupply, observed AI return/staging and a reviewed coastal-depth fix. Final headline Epic 379 turns (target 350-400), Long 342 versus prior 367, Standard 234 versus prior 223; all seven pacing cases have zero refused orders. 1,861 tests and nine affected browser journeys pass, as do typecheck, lint, content validation and production build; historical saves/replay remain exact. Primary master working tree is uncommitted; nothing published or deployed. Broad naval recovery and Standard/Long balance remain open. Evidence: ~/Work/Theandril/docs/development/prompt-reports/2026-09-23-fleet-provisions.md
